subject: Post-call: Knowledge-fit report & ops checklist for RAG pilot — Hartwell MedTech

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Knowledge-fit report & ops checklist for RAG pilot — Hartwell MedTech

Thanks again for taking time today, Caroline — quick recap and recommended next steps from our discovery so we can scope an initial RAG pilot. I pulled this together while it’s fresh.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Pilot model family: open Llama-3-70B-Chat quantized (q8_0) with Redwood-verified latency profile; fallback to Llama-3-13B for low-cost latency-sensitive routes.
- Retriever: hybrid BM25 + dense (FAISS hnsw) with document chunking at ~800 tokens.
- Reranker: lightweight cross-encoder (distil-cross-encoder-v1) for top-20 -> final top-5 re-ranking.

Why this stack: proven balance of recall and precision for technical docs, quantized large chat models keep cost reasonable while preserving instruction-following for summarization and QA. The distil cross-encoder reduces hallucination on short-answer tasks without bloating latency for your anticipated 500cpm volume.

Benchmarks & artifacts I attached:
- benchmark-results-20270417.csv: small-shot metrics from our sandbox eval on your sample docs (recall@5, mrr@10, grounding-precision).
- hartwell-prod-sample-docs.zip: anonymized documents you shared in the call (already redacted).
- SoW-draft-v1.pdf: an initial Statement of Work for a 6-week pilot (scope, success metrics, test plan).

Proposed evaluation plan (5 steps):
1) Ingest & normalization (2 business days): indexing with 800-token chunk hops, canonical metadata fields.
2) Baseline retrieval (3 days): BM25 + sparse-first pass, measure recall@20.
3) Dense indexing & reranker (5 days): FAISS build, tune hnsw params, run cross-encoder re-rank on top-20.
4) Prompt set & regression checks (3 days): create canonical prompts for QA, summarization, and snippet extraction; run regression harness vs your 50 seed queries.
5) Canary pilot (7 days): route 5% of internal test traffic to Redwood, measure grounding precision and latency SLA.

Key metrics we’ll track (pilot success criteria):
- Grounding precision >= 0.88 on the QA prompt set (definition: fraction of answers with direct evidence spans).
- Recall@20 >= 0.92 for QA queries derived from the R&D corpus.
- 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for user-facing short answers (model + reranker).
- No quality regressions across prompt set (we’ll create an alert if semantic similarity to baseline drops > 6%).

Data & security notes: we’ll use your VPC for private deployment if you want to keep content on-prem; otherwise we’ll run in Redwood Private with KMS integration and audit logs. Let us know which you prefer — this affects onboarding ETA.

Asks / immediate next steps:
- Caroline: share a HubSpot link to the primary procurement contact + any internal legal constraints (export controls, retention) by end of week.
- Caroline: confirm whether the pilot should be Private (VPC) or Hosted — default assumption in SoW is Hosted with customer redaction; change to Private will add ~5 business days.
- Ben/Markus: review SoW draft (attached) and confirm any technical redlines.

If that all sounds good I’ll: finalize SoW, schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday next week, and spin up the sandbox index with the sample docs so Ben can run the first benchmark.

Thanks — Monica

Subject: Re: Post-call: Knowledge-fit report & ops checklist for RAG pilot — Hartwell MedTech

Great questions — a few technical clarifications and the concrete plan on citations & reranker tuning.

Citations: we’ll implement evidence spans as token-offset anchors at ingestion time and surface both:
- character offsets (start/end) inside the original uploaded doc for precise traceability, and
- paragraph-level metadata (doc_id, chunk_id) for quick navigation.
Implementation detail: we store chunk-level start_char/end_char in the index; the QA pipeline returns the chunk plus exact span offsets extracted by the reader. That should satisfy engineers who need to open the source and locate the sentence quickly.

Retriever tuning notes:
- Sparse (BM25): increase k1 to 1.4 for your corpus (technical writing), use 0.8 for b to avoid overemphasizing long specs.
- Dense (FAISS hnsw): target ef_search=128 for stable recall@20, build ef_construction=200. Chunk hop size at 800 tokens with 128-token overlap.

Reranker rationale and config:
- Use distil-cross-encoder-v1 tuned on technical QA; it’s lighter than full cross-encoder while giving >12% uplift on grounding-precision in our tests. We’ll run re-ranker on top-20 from dense+sparse union and return top-5.
- Latency mitigation: run the cross-encoder in batched mode with a 50ms scheduling window to keep 95p latency within target under 500ms for the expected traffic profile.

Prompt sets and regression harness:
- I attached a seed prompt set (in the Drive link) with three categories: short-answer (fact extraction), synthesis (multi-paragraph summary), and procedure extraction (step lists). We’ll add your 15 edge queries.
- Regression check: we’ll compute semantic-similarity via pairwise embedding cosine against the baseline outputs and flag any prompt whose similarity drops > 0.06. Also monitor grounding delta per prompt.

Next ops items I’ll execute after we get VPC confirmation:
1) Provision VPC connector and KMS keys (3-4 business days).
2) Ingest sample docs into a customer sandbox (1-2 business days).
3) Run first benchmark and share a dashboard (recall/mrr/grounding-precision/latency) — aim to deliver by EOD Friday.

If you want, I can run an extra experiment swapping distil-cross-encoder for a token-classifier reranker (faster at infer time) but it reduces precision slightly; we can A/B in the canary.

—Ben
